title: Pushforward and pullback of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring ([det-def-sfb-condensed-ring]),
with pulled-back coefficient rings $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$
([det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]), categories of module objects
$\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ ([det-def-sfb-module-objects]) and coefficient morphisms
$\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$, $\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to f^{\Ab}_*\Lambda_X$
([det-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]) for morphisms of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$.
Everything below is stated for a general
$\Lambda$; the $\ell$-adic rings, including $\underline{\Qlb}$, are instances.
Write $f^{\Ab}_*$ and $f^*_{\Ab}$ for the pushforward and pullback of sheaves of
abelian groups ([def-sfb-finite-lower-star], [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] with
$\mathcal A=\Ab$); $f^{\Ab}_*$ is lax monoidal ([def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal])
and $f^*_{\Ab}$ is strong monoidal ([def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]), so both transport
module objects ([det-def-sfb-transport]); applied to ring objects such as
$\Lambda_Y$, the symbols $f^*$ and $f_*$ always mean these functors of abelian
sheaves. Every functor on module objects is "transport
the $\Ab$-valued functor, then change scalars along $\eta_f$ or $\alpha_f$"
([det-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]). For a morphism of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$:

- the *pushforward*
  $$
  f_*:=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)\colon
  \Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Y};
  $$
  the underlying sheaf of $f_*M$ is $f^{\Ab}_*M$, with $\Lambda_Y$ acting through
  $\eta_f$, and $f_*$ is additive and left exact;
- the *pullback*
  $$
  f^*:=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\colon
  \Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X},
  \qquad f^*M=\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M,
  $$
  the ringed-topos pullback. The extension of scalars along $\alpha_f$ is kept
  although $\alpha_f$ is invertible, so that the definition is the standard one and
  does not depend on a choice of inverse;
- the *adjunction* $f^*\dashv f_*$: the lift of the monoidal adjunction
  $f^*_{\Ab}\dashv f^{\Ab}_*$ ([lem-sfb-finite-monoidal-adjunction]) to module objects, composed with
  $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f}$, using that
  $\eta_f$ is the mate of $\alpha_f$;
- for $g\colon Y\to Z$, the *composition isomorphisms*
  $$
  g_*\circ f_*\cong(g\circ f)_*,\qquad (g\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ g^*,
  $$
  the first lifting the composition isomorphism of pushforwards of abelian sheaves
  ([def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]),
  the second deduced from the first by uniqueness of left adjoints.

The constructions use only $\alpha_f$, $\eta_f$ and the mate relation between
them; that $\alpha_f$ is invertible enters proofs about these functors (exactness,
the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$), not their definitions.

proof.text: For any commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$ and any scheme morphism $f$, take the functor $f_*$ of [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Its statement supplies precisely $\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\operatorname{mapMod}(f_*^{\Ab})$, the underlying abelian sheaf, the action through $\eta_f$, additivity and left exactness. Take $f^*$ of [def-sfb-module-upper-star]; its defining formula is $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})=\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}(-)$. Thus both functors use the forward coefficient morphisms and the stated module-object categories.

Apply [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] to the same $\Lambda$ and $f$. It gives the composite of the lifted monoidal adjunction and extension/restriction adjunction, identifying its right adjoint with step 1. The mate relation needed for that identification is exactly $\eta_f=f_*^{\Ab}(\alpha_f)u_{\Lambda_Y}$ in [det-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. The resulting natural bijection identifies $\Lambda_X$-linear maps $\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M\to N$ with $\Lambda_Y$-linear maps $M\to f_*N$, giving $f^*\dashv f_*$.

For composable $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$, [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp] gives the natural module isomorphism $g_*f_*\cong(gf)_*$ with precisely the underlying abelian-sheaf composition comparison $c$. Its compatibility inputs are available with these same morphisms: [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal] applies with $\mathcal A=\Ab$ and says that $c$ is monoidal, while [lem-sfb-eta-comp] says $\eta_{gf}=c_{\Lambda_X}g_*^{\Ab}(\eta_f)\eta_g$. The latter uses the canonical pullback-composition comparisons and coefficient mates, as in the coefficient morphisms of the statement; it imposes no geometric or coefficient restriction beyond the ones here. These are exactly the comparison and scalar maps in the cited module-composition definition.

source.place: second and third sentences: pushforward composition and its compatibility inputs

proof.text: With the adjunctions of step 2 and the pushforward comparison of step 3, [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] gives the unique natural isomorphism $(gf)^*\cong f^*g^*$ whose forward map is the mate of $c:g_*f_*\to(gf)_*$. Its inverse is the mate of $c^{-1}$, so the directions agree with the displayed comparison in this item. This is the required uniqueness-of-left-adjoints construction.

The coefficient morphism $\alpha_f$ is an isomorphism by [det-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Nevertheless the formula in step 1 extends scalars along the forward map $\alpha_f$: the defining coequalizer in clause 2 of [det-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] uses only that map, and the adjunction in step 2 uses its mate. Hence none of these constructions requires choosing an inverse to $\alpha_f$.
